script.opening_words: You're ignoring the biggest investor in your life, and I can prove it with one sentence. Every 2 weeks, someone deposits thousands of dollars into your account expecting nothing in return except your time, and you're treating them like an ATM instead of a venture capital firm that's trying to make you rich. I'm Nick, and I've spent the last decade watching people stumble backward into wealth while thinking they were just showing up to work. The math is so
script.ending_words: a corporate partnership. The real scam isn't that jobs under pay you, the real scam is that most people never realize their job is the best investor they'll ever have offering free capital, tax advantages, and institutional backing. And they walk away from it chasing freedom they haven't funded yet. Don't be most people, extract everything, build quietly, leave when the math says you can, not when your feelings do.
script.analysis: Full 19505 canonical characters read. Employer-as-investor reframe: hook, 401(k) match as 100% ROI, HSA triple tax, education benefits as grants, salary as seed funding, benefits ~30% claim, $80K benefits tally and 30-year compounding, "shadow portfolio" resource extraction (software, networks, time arbitrage), credibility/stability/optionality, 10-year hypothetical (65K->80K, condo, HELOC, three rentals, $600K net worth), job switching, $45K objection, escape velocity, close. Correct: match/HSA mechanics, most arithmetic reproduces. Wrong or misleading: benefits as % of salary (wrong denominator and includes mandatory benefits), education/wellness counted as investable, aggressive real-estate path, "millions" from job loyalty, "time arbitrage" on employer time. Stored ending complete.
beat_map: Hook: your employer is your biggest investor.
401(k) match as 100% ROI; one-third miss it.
ATM vs venture capital; cap table metaphor.

claim_audit.assessment: BLSECEC: benefits are ~29.9% of total compensation (wages 70.1%), i.e. ~43% of wages, so "30% of base salary" uses the wrong denominator; the share includes legally required Social Security, Medicare, UI and workers' comp that employees cannot "capture".
